findings.text: Generic return code BPF_OK means success with value 0 while BPF_DROP means drop with value 2 and BPF_REDIRECT means redirect with value 7. Value 1 plus values 3 through 6 stay reserved. Values above 127 stay reserved for program type use, with BPF_LWT_REROUTE at 128 signalling reroute on mutated layer three headers and BPF_FLOW_DISSECTOR_CONTINUE at 129 requesting fallback to the standard dissector.

Socket view bpf_sock orders bound_dev_if, family, type, protocol, mark and priority as 32 bit unsigned values. It continues with src_ip4 as 32 bit unsigned and src_ip6 as four 32 bit words, then src_port as 32 bit host order and dst_port as 16 bit network order with 16 bits of unnamed padding. It ends with dst_ip4 as 32 bit unsigned, dst_ip6 as four 32 bit words, state as 32 bit unsigned and rx_queue_mapping as 32 bit signed.

TCP diagnostic view bpf_tcp_sock holds snd_cwnd, srtt_us, rtt_min, snd_ssthresh, rcv_nxt, snd_nxt, snd_una, mss_cache, ecn_flags, rate_delivered, rate_interval_us, packets_out, retrans_out, total_retrans, segs_in, data_segs_in, segs_out, data_segs_out, lost_out and sacked_out as 32 bit unsigned in that order, then bytes_received and bytes_acked as 64 bit unsigned, then dsack_dups, delivered, delivered_ce and icsk_retransmits as 32 bit unsigned.

Smoothed round trip is stored scaled by eight in microseconds, with separate minimum. Rate sample pairs delivered count with elapsed microseconds. Segment counters distinguish total versus data only for both directions. The two 64 bit byte totals accumulate acknowledged sequence advances for receive and send. Delivered counts include retransmissions, with a separate exclusively congestion experienced total, while DSACK dupes and unrecovered timeouts track loss recovery.

Tuple container bpf_sock_tuple offers an anonymous union with two address family shapes. The IPv4 shape named ipv4 holds saddr and daddr as 32 bit big endian plus sport and dport as 16 bit values. The IPv6 shape named ipv6 holds saddr and daddr as four 32 bit big endian words each plus sport and dport as 16 bit values.
Traffic control return base TCX_NEXT requests continuation with value negative one, TCX_PASS accepts with 0, TCX_DROP discards with 2 and TCX_REDIRECT forwards with 7.
Redirect target bpf_xdp_sock carries a single 32 bit unsigned queue_id selecting the receive queue.
Packet headroom constant XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM fixes 256 bytes of leading space for receive processing.
Packet verdict XDP_ABORTED holds 0 for exceptional abort, XDP_DROP holds 1 for discard, XDP_PASS holds 2 for pass, XDP_TX holds 3 for transmit and XDP_REDIRECT holds 4 for redirect.

Packet context xdp_md carries data, data_end and data_meta as 32 bit offsets delimiting packet and metadata ranges. It adds ingress_ifindex for receive device, rx_queue_index for receive queue and egress_ifindex for transmit device, each 32 bit unsigned.

Device map value bpf_devmap_val pairs 32 bit unsigned ifindex with an anonymous union bpf_prog holding either fd as signed 32 bit program descriptor on writes or id as 32 bit unsigned program identifier on reads.

CPU map value bpf_cpumap_val pairs 32 bit unsigned qsize for remote queue depth with an anonymous union bpf_prog holding either fd as signed descriptor on writes or id as unsigned identifier on reads.
Socket verdict SK_DROP holds 0 for discard and SK_PASS holds 1 for pass.

Message context sk_msg_md opens with data and data_end as context pointers bounding readable bytes. It continues with family as 32 bit unsigned, remote_ip4 and local_ip4 as 32 bit addresses, remote_ip6 and local_ip6 as four word addresses, remote_port in network order and local_port in host order, plus 32 bit unsigned size for total message length, closing with sk as context pointer to the current socket.

Reuseport selection context sk_reuseport_md opens with data and data_end pointers and 32 bit unsigned len for total packet length from transport header. It adds eth_protocol in network order, ip_protocol, bind_inany flag for wildcard bind, and hash of the four tuple, each 32 bit unsigned. It closes with sk pointing at a group member and migrating_sk pointing at the socket needing migration when present, both as context pointers.
Tag length constant BPF_TAG_SIZE fixes eight bytes for program tags.

Program introspection record bpf_prog_info starts with 32 bit unsigned type and id, then tag as eight byte array sized by the tag constant. It follows with jited_prog_len and xlated_prog_len as 32 bit lengths plus jited_prog_insns and xlated_prog_insns as aligned 64 bit user addresses. It continues with load_time as 64 bit boot relative nanoseconds, created_by_uid as 32 bit identifier, nr_map_ids count with map_ids address, fixed length name bytes, ifindex as 32 bit device index, a single bit gpl_compatible flag with 31 bits padding, netns_dev and netns_ino as 64 bit namespace cookies, then nr_jited_ksyms and nr_jited_func_lens counts with jited_ksyms and jited_func_lens addresses.

It continues with btf_id and func_info_rec_size as 32 bit values plus func_info address and nr_func_info count, then nr_line_info count with line_info and jited_line_info addresses and nr_jited_line_info count. Next are line_info_rec_size and jited_line_info_rec_size as 32 bit record sizes, nr_prog_tags count with prog_tags address, run_time_ns, run_cnt and recursion_misses as 64 bit runtime totals, verified_insns as 32 bit count, attach_btf_obj_id and attach_btf_id as 32 bit attach identifiers, 32 bits padding, with the whole record aligned to eight bytes.

Map introspection record bpf_map_info orders type, id, key_size, value_size, max_entries and map_flags as 32 bit unsigned, then fixed length name bytes and 32 bit unsigned ifindex plus btf_vmlinux_value_type_id. It continues with netns_dev and netns_ino as 64 bit cookies, btf_id, btf_key_type_id, btf_value_type_id and btf_vmlinux_id as 32 bit identifiers, map_extra as 64 bit extension, hash as aligned address with hash_size as 32 bit length and 32 bits padding, aligned to eight bytes.

BTF introspection record bpf_btf_info pairs btf address as aligned 64 bit with btf_size as 32 bit length and id as 32 bit identifier, then name address with name_len as 32 bit length and kernel_btf as 32 bit flag, aligned to eight bytes.

Link record bpf_link_info starts with type, id and prog_id as 32 bit unsigned, then a discriminated union. Member raw_tracepoint carries tp_name address with tp_name_len plus cookie. Member tracing carries attach_type with target_obj_id and target_btf_id plus cookie. Member cgroup carries cgroup_id with attach_type. Member iter carries target_name address with target_name_len plus map choice with map_id and a second choice offering either cgroup_id with order or tid with pid. Member netns carries netns_ino with attach_type, member xdp carries ifindex, member struct_ops carries map_id, and member netfilter carries pf, hooknum, signed priority and flags.

Union continues with kprobe_multi holding addrs, count, flags, missed and cookies, and uprobe_multi holding path, offsets, ref_ctr_offsets and cookies with path_size, count, flags and pid. Member tracing_multi holds attach_type, count and btf_obj_id with ids, addrs and cookies. Member perf_event holds type plus a nested choice among uprobe with file_name, name_len, offset, cookie and ref_ctr_offset, kprobe with func_name, name_len, offset, addr, missed and cookie, tracepoint with tp_name, name_len and cookie, and event with config, type and cookie. Members tcx and netkit each hold ifindex with attach_type, sockmap holds map_id with attach_type, with the record aligned to eight bytes.
Token capability record bpf_token_info holds allowed_cmds, allowed_maps, allowed_progs and allowed_attachs as 64 bit masks, aligned to eight bytes.

Introspection records use aligned 64 bit address fields for user buffers and counts that pair with them, with eight byte overall alignment ensuring stable layout across architectures. Length and count fields serve as in-out sizes that the kernel updates to actual use.

Address rewrite context bpf_sock_addr orders user_family, user_ip4, user_ip6 as four words and user_port, then family, type and protocol, then msg_src_ip4 with msg_src_ip6 as four words, each 32 bit unsigned, closing with sk as context pointer to the socket.

Rewrite context enforces per field widths and orders. User family plus family, type and protocol permit 32 bit reads without writes. User port and four byte message source permit one, two or four byte reads with four byte writes, while sixteen byte address storage permits one, two, four or eight byte reads with four or eight byte writes. All address and port bytes use network order.

Socket operations context bpf_sock_ops starts with 32 bit unsigned op selecting the callback, plus a shared union offering args as four 32 bit inputs, reply as 32 bit output or replylong as four 32 bit outputs. It continues with family, remote_ip4, local_ip4, remote_ip6 and local_ip6 as address storage, remote_port in network order and local_port in host order, is_fullsock gate, then snd_cwnd, srtt_us, bpf_sock_ops_cb_flags, state, rtt_min, snd_ssthresh, rcv_nxt, snd_nxt, snd_una, mss_cache, ecn_flags, rate_delivered, rate_interval_us, packets_out, retrans_out, total_retrans, segs_in, data_segs_in, segs_out, data_segs_out, lost_out and sacked_out as 32 bit values.

It continues with sk_txhash as 32 bit hash, bytes_received and bytes_acked as 64 bit totals, sk as socket pointer, skb_data and skb_data_end as packet window pointers, skb_len as 32 bit total length, skb_tcp_flags as 32 bit flag copy and skb_hwtstamp as 64 bit hardware stamp.

Operations context gates TCP metrics on is_fullsock, reading as zero without a full socket. Addresses use network order, remote port uses network order while local port uses host order. Packet window skb_data to skb_data_end covers only the transport header, with availability varying by operation and flag copy remaining valid even when reservation precedes header construction.

Flag BPF_SOCK_OPS_RTO_CB_FLAG is bit zero, BPF_SOCK_OPS_RETRANS_CB_FLAG is bit one, BPF_SOCK_OPS_STATE_CB_FLAG is bit two, BPF_SOCK_OPS_RTT_CB_FLAG is bit three, BPF_SOCK_OPS_PARSE_ALL_HDR_OPT_CB_FLAG is bit four, BPF_SOCK_OPS_PARSE_UNKNOWN_HDR_OPT_CB_FLAG is bit five and BPF_SOCK_OPS_WRITE_HDR_OPT_CB_FLAG is bit six, with BPF_SOCK_OPS_ALL_CB_FLAGS covering all as 127.
Timestamp control SK_BPF_CB_TX_TIMESTAMPING enables transmit stamping with value 1, with SK_BPF_CB_MASK covering valid bits as 1.

Operation selector starts at BPF_SOCK_OPS_VOID for no operation, then BPF_SOCK_OPS_TIMEOUT_INIT for initial retransmit timeout and BPF_SOCK_OPS_RWND_INIT for initial window, each returning negative one for default. Next are BPF_SOCK_OPS_TCP_CONNECT_CB before active open, BPF_SOCK_OPS_ACTIVE_ESTABLISHED_CB and BPF_SOCK_OPS_PASSIVE_ESTABLISHED_CB at establishment, BPF_SOCK_OPS_NEEDS_ECN for congestion control query and BPF_SOCK_OPS_BASE_RTT for path threshold. Notifications follow with BPF_SOCK_OPS_RTO_CB carrying retransmit count, timeout and expiry, BPF_SOCK_OPS_RETRANS_CB carrying sequence, segment count and transmit status, BPF_SOCK_OPS_STATE_CB carrying old and new states, BPF_SOCK_OPS_TCP_LISTEN_CB at listen entry and BPF_SOCK_OPS_RTT_CB carrying measured and smoothed round trip.

Header option sequence uses BPF_SOCK_OPS_PARSE_HDR_OPT_CB for inbound parsing, BPF_SOCK_OPS_HDR_OPT_LEN_CB for space reservation and BPF_SOCK_OPS_WRITE_HDR_OPT_CB for outbound writing, with reservation and writing carrying a cookie request flag for synchronisation cases. Timestamp stages use BPF_SOCK_OPS_TSTAMP_SCHED_CB at device queueing, BPF_SOCK_OPS_TSTAMP_SND_SW_CB before hand to hardware, BPF_SOCK_OPS_TSTAMP_SND_HW_CB in hardware, BPF_SOCK_OPS_TSTAMP_ACK_CB when a send call is acknowledged and BPF_SOCK_OPS_TSTAMP_SENDMSG_CB per send system call for correlation.

Socket facing views mix orders by field. Source ports and local ports use host order while destination ports, remote ports and all address bytes use network order. Consumers must convert before comparison across the two orders.

Several fields change meaning by direction or require caller sizing. Device and CPU map program references interpret as descriptor on write but identifier on read. Name, address, offset and cookie pointers need caller buffers whose length or count fields update on return, so undersized buffers truncate. Reuseport accessible bytes may be shorter than total length, requiring helper reads for the tail.

These definitions form stable userspace programming interfaces for packet verdicts, socket views, map values, message contexts and introspection records, consumed by control tools and by in kernel program contexts.
